inventory.facts: One graph, no subfigures, no table, no grid, no apparatus. Horizontal rightward velocity axis and vertical upward mass axis share one origin.
requirements: Preserve one shared coordinate frame and both positive-direction arrowheads.

inventory.facts: Vertical axis is labelled m above its arrow. Horizontal axis is labelled v near its right arrow. The origin is labelled O below-left of the axes crossing.
requirements: Do not conflate the coordinate origin (zero mass) with the nonzero rest-mass intercept.

inventory.facts: The curve meets the mass axis at the tick labelled m0, above O. Higher labelled ticks are 2m0, 3m0, 4m0, 5m0, 6m0, 7m0, 8m0 with approximately equal vertical spacing.
requirements: Preserve the rest-mass intercept at v=0 and m=m0.
Use m0 as the mass scale rather than inventing kilograms or an absolute mass.

inventory.facts: The speed axis has small roughly equally spaced ticks between O and c, a labelled halfway tick 0.5c, and a labelled c position below the near-vertical right-hand feature. The axis itself continues right past c.
requirements: Preserve the labelled halfway and c positions and their common speed scale.
An axis extending past c must not imply that the physical curve exists at or beyond c.

inventory.facts: One solid curve begins at the m0 intercept, is nearly horizontal initially, then rises increasingly steeply toward the c position. It reaches the top of the displayed mass range near the c line. No isolated terminal-point marker is drawn.
requirements: Preserve monotonic growth for the nonnegative speed branch.
The visible upper truncation is not a finite physical endpoint.
Compare numerical samples and the allowable domain to the authoritative corrected text, not to scan stroke thickness or a vaguely similar curve.

inventory.facts: A thin vertical ink feature aligns with the c tick, most clearly visible down to the horizontal axis beneath the steep upper curve. The scan does not explicitly label this feature as an asymptote, nor does it supply a reachable mass value at c.
requirements: If modern output explicitly marks an asymptote, declare that clarification as an addition.
Never draw a closed curve endpoint at v=c.

inventory.facts: There is no displayed formula, legend, measured dot series, cultural imagery, or verbal explanatory text. The figure-number caption is not present in this canonical crop.
requirements: Declare added formulas, explanatory English labels, normalized notation, or guide styling as modern additions rather than source pixels.

numericInterpretationLimit: Only the labelled origin, rest-mass intercept, mass multiples, 0.5c and c are directly inventoried as numerical source facts. The hand-drawn curve is not a calibrated table; exact intermediate values must follow the authoritative m=m0/sqrt(1-v^2/c^2) relation supplied for this review.
